name: Ireland: check of forms and supplied documents
source: https://trialagents.com/ctis/ireland/en/part-ii-document-checklist (reviewed 23 September 2026), items 1 and 5-13 and 'Submission checks that prevent avoidable RFIs'

common.check: Trial title and EU trial number (if assigned) match the protocol and CTIS.
Every field the assistant answers is answered; fields that belong to the site, investigator, insurer or sponsor are left empty, not invented.
In English; signature only where the Irish rule for that document requires it (none at submission for K1, M1, M2, P1, S1; N1 and R1 follow the national form's authorisation fields).
CTIS title follows the naming guide and requirements.json; accessible, searchable Word file or original PDF, not an image-only scan.

IE-K1.check: Uses the EU Recruitment and Informed Consent Procedure template version 2.0 for a new Part II submission from 1 September 2026 (initial, additional Member State, Article 11 completion).
Identification of potential participants, first act of recruitment, initial approach, access to medical records or patient lists, privacy protection and who informs and takes consent are described.
Consent takers are the investigator or a registered medical practitioner, dentist or nurse designated by the investigator, with role, training, setting, timing and understanding checks.

The yes/no answers for incapacitated adults, minors, impartial witness and emergency match the project's populations and study facts; each 'yes' section is completed and each 'no' section gives the not-applicable answer.

Incapacitated adults: Irish legally designated representative hierarchy, participant involvement and refusal, capacity assessment and reassessment, separate data-processing route (HRCDC where needed), re-consent when capacity returns.
Minors: under 16, verified guardian authority, assent, refusal respected, re-consent at 16.
Impartial witness: reason, selection, independence, attendance for the full discussion, attestation and witness signature field.
Emergency: every Article 35 condition, therapeutic window, attempts to locate a representative, consent follow-up, Irish data-processing route.
Each recruitment item (K2) is described with how it is used and how responses from people who are not eligible are handled.

IE-M1.check: One current CV per principal investigator and Irish site, in the EU or an equivalent NREC-aligned format.
Shows education, training and relevant experience, professional registration as a registered medical practitioner or registered dentist, and clinical-trial experience.
Name, site and date fields completed by the investigator; investigator name and site match CTIS and every form.

IE-M2-DOI.check: One trial-specific declaration per principal investigator and Irish site identifying any economic, institutional or personal interest that could affect impartiality.
Investigator, institution and date fields completed by the investigator; not signed (not required).

IE-N1.check: The current NREC-CT Site Suitability Form is used for every Irish site, not only the generic EU form.
Describes the site, facilities, equipment, procedures, staffing, expertise, pharmacy arrangements and site-specific issues.
Research exposure to ionising radiation is addressed in the site form.
Issuer, position, organisation and date fields completed and the national form's authorisation field followed.
Planned participant number matches CTIS and the Irish site list; site and investigator names match CTIS and every form.

IE-O1.check: Valid insurance certificate or evidence of an appropriate indemnity arrangement, appropriate to the nature and extent of trial risk and providing compensation for damage resulting from participation.
Cover dates valid for the planned trial period; renewal explained where cover expires earlier.
State Claims Agency guidance and the Clinical Trial Indemnity Form checked for delegated State authority healthcare enterprises and academic institutions.
Injury and insurance wording in the participant documents matches the evidence.

IE-P1.check: Present as a disclosure even when no payment is offered (states so).
States whether participants, parents, carers or legal representatives receive travel, meals, accommodation, loss-of-earnings reimbursement, money or non-monetary items.
No incentives for minors, incapacitated adults or breastfeeding women beyond expenses or loss of earnings directly related to participation; any token of appreciation flagged for ethics review.

Healthy volunteers: reimbursement of expenses separated from payment for time and inconvenience; amount, schedule, tax position if known and payment after early withdrawal stated; not contingent on completing every procedure.
Compensation, travel and third-party reimbursement details match every participant document.

IE-P2.check: Describes financing, payments to investigators and sites, and other agreements that could affect impartiality.
A contract is uploaded only if the requested information is not otherwise provided or NREC-CT asks for it.
Financial statements, participant documents and the reimbursement process agree.

IE-R1.check: The current NREC Statement of Compliance regarding Data Protection (version 2 at the review date) is used, or a DPIA is provided instead; the generic EU GDPR statement is not used as a substitute.

Identifies controllers, processors, recipients, lawful bases, the Article 9 condition, Irish Health Research Regulations safeguards, retention, transfers, security, participant rights and Data Protection Officer input.
The national template's completion and authorisation fields are followed.
Retention, recipients, transfers, withdrawal and the data-processing route agree with the SIS/ICF, protocol, S1 and any HRCDC application or decision.

IE-S1.check: EU biological-samples template or accepted NREC equivalent, present when samples are collected, accessed, stored, transferred or planned for future use.
Sample type and volume, collection, legal responsibility, analysis, storage location and duration, coding, access, transfers, destruction and future use are described.

Future use: limited to a described disease, health or research area, later ethics review, recontact where the purpose cannot be described; consistent with the separate secondary-use consent (Section 5, f03).
Storage, retention, recipients, transfers and withdrawal wording agree with the protocol, SIS/ICF and R1.

IE-FEE.check: Commercial sponsor: completed HPRA fee application form and proof of payment are in the CTIS Forms section (proof of fee payment), not in Part II K to S.
Non-commercial or academic trial: no fee evidence is planned (not charged).
